clips.text_zh: 又係另一個狗幣上岸然後廢咗嘅故事。22歲炒狗幣溝女旅行dropout買咗condo，依家27做返個返學返工嘅奴工。咁我地呢啲30歲仲輸緊嘅算咩。感覺似loop緊。不過我無condod，最少無供樓壓力lol
clips.text_en_b1: In 2021 when I was 22, I made a bunch of random crypto money from Dogecoin. I lived for two years with no job, on a perma vacation. I dropped out of school and bought a condo for $230K. The money ran out. I went back to school, graduated, and now I make $100K living in my condo.
clips.source_hint: Anon on /biz/ who cashed out crypto into a condo and now feels stuck

signal.rationale: Pure loss-pain storytelling, no trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Back in 2021, when I was 22, I struck it rich on Dogecoin out of sheer luck. For roughly two years I dropped out of uni, bought a $230K condo, and essentially lived a perma-vacation lifestyle. The gravy train eventually dried up, so I went back, finished my degree, and now at 27 I'm grinding a $100K salary just to keep up with the mortgage. Meanwhile student loans and credit card debt keep piling on.
clips.text_en_c1: Back in 2021, when I was twenty-two, I made a substantial amount on Dogecoin essentially by accident. For the next two years, I lived without employment, effectively on an extended holiday; I dropped out of university and used the proceeds to put a down payment on a $230,000 condo. The windfall eventually dried up, forcing me to enrol again, finish my degree, and settle into a salaried position that pays roughly $100,000 a year. I am now twenty-seven, and what troubles me is the sense that I have merely traded one treadmill for another.
clips.text_en_c2: At twenty-two, I parlayed a serendipitous Dogecoin windfall into what I mistook for financial sovereignty: two indolent years of perpetual travel, an abandoned degree, and a $230,000 condominium purchased on the assumption that the carnival would never end. It did, of course, as such affairs invariably do. I returned to university, graduated, and now at twenty-seven inhabit a modest $100,000 salary shackled to the very asset I once considered liberation. The Sisyphean rhythm of work, consumption, repetition has become my unexamined default. Student loans and credit-card balances accrue in the background. I do, however, take grim consolation in the absence of mortgage obligations.

clips.text_zh: 十年長揸只揸一樣，你揀BTC定黃金？我兩樣都揸緊，黃金係long-term hedge，BTC就係prop firm嗰邊賭身家。我揀BTC，原因好簡單，美國放水周期嚟緊gold都會升但BTC會爆。法蘭克福嗰邊印銀紙印到傻。
clips.text_en_b1: Bitcoin vs Gold. If you had to hold only one for the next 10 years, would you choose Bitcoin or gold? What makes your choice better than the other? Serious answers only, no cope. Gold bugs keep saying BTC is a bubble, but the supply is fixed at 21 million while central banks print forever. I'm picking BTC. The next decade is digital.
clips.source_hint: Classic /biz/ 10-year hold debate, Bitcoin vs gold

signal.rationale: OP explicitly picks BTC over gold for 10-year hold, framing it as digital scarcity play

clips.text_en_b2: If you had to hold a single asset for the next ten years, would you go with Bitcoin or gold? Gold bugs love hammering on about BTC being a bubble, yet they conveniently overlook that Bitcoin's supply is hard-capped at 21 million while central banks, Frankfurt included, keep the printing presses running overtime. Although gold tends to climb during liquidity cycles, BTC tends to absolutely rip when money printer goes brrr.
clips.text_en_c1: The question that genuinely interests me is whether, over a ten-year horizon, one should hold Bitcoin or gold exclusively. Gold advocates will insist that Bitcoin is a speculative bubble destined to collapse, yet their argument ignores a fundamental asymmetry: Bitcoin's supply is mathematically capped at twenty-one million coins, whereas central banks, particularly the Federal Reserve and the ECB, continue to expand their balance sheets with apparent impunity. Frankfurt's money printer has been operating at full tilt, and although gold will almost certainly appreciate during the next liquidity cycle, I am convinced that Bitcoin's upside is categorically different in magnitude.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial decadal wager: Bitcoin or gold? Gold bugs persist in proclaiming BTC a speculative bubble, conveniently overlooking that its supply is mathematically capped at twenty-one million while central banks—the Frankfurt contingent chief among them—dilute fiat with industrial alacrity. Gold constitutes a prudent long-term hedge against monetary incontinence; Bitcoin, by contrast, is the asymmetric bet, the bet that one ought to size accordingly. Should the forthcoming liquidity cycle materialise as anticipated, bullion shall certainly appreciate, but BTC shall, if my thesis holds, ascend by an order of magnitude. The next decade, contra the nostalgia of the gold lobby, is emphatically digital. I choose accordingly.

clips.text_zh: /g/問：你仲有咩係AGI做唔好嘅？老實講我諗唔到。考HKIE都係要記spec同formula，AI做律師做工程師只係時間問題。咁我30歲先轉行係咪已經輸晒？🙏
clips.text_en_b1: What can you do that the newest OpenAI AGI model can't do better? Seriously, I've been thinking about this all night. I used to think being good at math or coding mattered. Now I'm not so sure. If it can pass the bar exam and write working code, what exactly is my edge? Tell me anons, what do you still have?
clips.source_hint: Existential /g/ thread asking what humans still beat AGI at
clips.text_en_b2: What exactly can you do that the latest OpenAGI model can't handle better? I've been wrestling with this question for hours. Skills that once felt secure, such as passing the bar exam or cranking out working code, no longer seem like a reliable edge. If AI can ace legal bar exams and ship clean functions, then what exactly am I bringing to the table? Hit me with honest answers, anons. What do you figure is still left for us?
clips.text_en_c1: I have been wrestling with this question for the better part of a week and, frankly, I am struggling to identify a skill I possess that the latest OpenAI model cannot replicate at a superior level. I once believed that mathematical reasoning and software engineering conferred a durable competitive advantage, but that conviction has eroded considerably. If these systems can already pass professional bar examinations and produce production-grade code, what precisely remains of human differentiation? I am told that judgment, creativity, and interpersonal nuance constitute my edge, yet even those claims feel increasingly tenuous the more I examine them.
clips.text_en_c2: I have been ruminating, somewhat queasily, on the question posed: what remains within the exclusive purview of human cognition now that frontier models can dispatch the bar examination, compose functional code, and memorise technical specifications with wearying proficiency? I once consoled myself that mathematical facility or programming acumen constituted defensible moats; that conviction has eroded considerably. If a sufficiently capable system can litigate, engineer, and iterate on its own architectures, what residual edge does a mid-career professional possess? Anons, I entreat you: identify, with brutal honesty, any skill or trait that has not yet been reduced to a token-weighted probability distribution.

clips.text_zh: Doge checks、tariffs、平油平餸、無人再送死去打猶太佬戰爭、Day 1放Epstein files。睇返美股期貨又係低開lol。又係嗰套，講就天下無敵，做就……不過我而家short緊NQ搏下，希望今次唔好再中伏🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Fell for it again. The DOGE checks. The tariffs. Cheap gas and groceries. No more Americans dying in Jewish wars in the Middle East. Release the Epstein files on day 1. Sound familiar? I keep buying the dip on hopium and getting wrecked. Someone please explain why I keep doing this to myself. NQ puts loading.

signal.rationale: Observational, political cope, no actionable trade despite tone

clips.text_en_b2: Fell for the hype yet again. DOGE stimulus checks, sweeping tariffs, cheap gas and groceries, no more Americans getting shipped off to die in foreign wars, and the Epstein files dropped on day one. Sounds familiar, right? Equity futures are pointing lower at the open, so here we go. I keep buying dips powered by pure hopium and getting wrecked for my trouble. NQ puts are loading. Someone talk me off the ledge before I do it again.
clips.text_en_c1: I have fallen for the same narrative cycle yet again, and I am frankly embarrassed by how predictable the pattern has become. The promised DOGE stimulus cheques, the sweeping tariffs, affordable fuel and groceries, an end to American entanglement in Middle Eastern conflicts, and the release of the Epstein files on day one. Equities futures, predictably, opened lower. I keep purchasing drawdowns fuelled by little more than wishful thinking and subsequently endure the consequences. What I find genuinely puzzling is the psychological mechanism that compels me to repeat this behaviour despite ample evidence suggesting I should know better.
clips.text_en_c2: Once more, the ritual humiliation. The promised DOGE disbursements, the theatrical tariffs, the affordable petrol and groceries, the cessation of foreign entanglements, the inaugural release of the Epstein files—a catalogue of sanguine pledges that would not, I now recognise with grim familiarity, survive contact with the legislative process. Equity futures gapped lower at the open, as they invariably do when rhetoric confronts reality. I have, against my better judgement, loaded NASDAQ puts, hoping that this particular cycle of optimism and subsequent disappointment shall prove, for once, profitably asymmetric. The lesson, evidently, refuses to stick.

clips.text_zh: 305M美金開發budget，仲未計marketing。LoL S15嘅skin都係milking吓，一個Legendary skin幾百蚊我仲要買埋傳說造型。Sum Ho問我點解唔儲錢，我答佢：『我儲緊一個Ahri chroma。』考牌溫書都無咁燒錢wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: 305 million dollar development budget. Excluding marketing costs. According to leaked documents. Amazing what they can achieve these days. I remember when games cost $60 to make and shipped complete. Now we get 70/100 metacritic scores and battle passes that drain your wallet. Where did it all go wrong? Probably the CEO's third yacht.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread about leaked AAA game dev budgets

signal.rationale: Observational, gaming industry rant, no trade

clips.text_en_b2: A $305 million development budget, not even counting marketing spend, according to leaked internal documents. Pretty wild what studios pull off these days. I grew up when games shipped complete for sixty bucks and nobody blinked. Now we're stuck shelling out for battle passes, overpriced Legendary skins, and chromas that nickel-and-dime you into oblivion. Meanwhile the CEO is busy furnishing his third yacht. I genuinely wonder where it all went sideways.
clips.text_en_c1: A development budget of $305 million, and that figure does not even encompass marketing expenditure, has been circulating via leaked internal documents. The sums involved are frankly staggering when one considers what they ostensibly produce. There was an era, not particularly distant, when a title could be developed for a fraction of that cost and shipped in a complete, polished state. What we receive instead are seventy-out-of-one-hundred Metacritic scores and battle pass systems engineered to extract incremental revenue indefinitely. Where, precisely, has the disconnect occurred? One suspects the answer involves executive compensation packages, shareholder obligations, and perhaps a third yacht, though these explanations offer cold comfort to consumers subsidising the…
clips.text_en_c2: Three hundred and five million dollars in development expenditure—marketing costs conspicuously excluded—per leaked internal documentation. One contemplates, with a mixture of incredulity and resignation, what such a budget ostensibly procures: titles that metastasise into live-service platforms, Metacritic aggregates hovering around seventy, and cosmetic ecosystems engineered to extract incremental revenue from a captive audience. The S15 League of Legends skin catalogue exemplifies the model; a single Legendary-tier skin and accompanying chroma constitutes, by my calculation, a more significant financial commitment than my driving instructor's entire lesson package. Where precisely did the industry err? Perhaps the third yacht holds the answer.

clips.text_zh: /fit/有個膠問：佢同identical twin食一樣嘢、量過大便calories都一樣，點解一個肥一個瘦。咁咪同我同肥仔信一樣。佢食極唔肥，我食水都肥lol。命理嗰邊sifu話係命，唔關代謝事。OK我信埋一份。
clips.text_en_b1: I have an identical twin brother. He is lean. I am fat. We measured how much we eat and the calorie measurement is identical. The dietary fat, protein, and carbs are all identical. We also collected our faeces and incinerated it, and it had an identical calorie measurement. What is causing me to be obese while my brother is lean?
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread on identical twin with same intake, different body
clips.text_en_b2: I've got an identical twin and we're at complete opposites. He's lean, I'm overweight, even though we eat the exact same meals and our calorie intake is identical. Fat, protein, carbs, everything matches up. We even went as far as collecting and incinerating our faeces to measure caloric output, and the readings came back identical. So what on earth explains why I'm obese while my brother stays ripped? Could it genuinely come down to plain genetics?
clips.text_en_c1: I share an identical genetic inheritance with my twin brother, and yet our physiques diverge dramatically. He remains lean while I have struggled with obesity for years, despite the fact that we consume essentially identical quantities of food. To rule out the obvious variables, we meticulously measured everything, from caloric intake to macronutrient composition, and even went so far as to collect and incinerate our faeces in a calorimeter. The results were indistinguishable across both samples. I have consulted endocrinologists, reviewed the relevant metabolic literature, and spoken to practitioners of traditional Chinese medicine, who invariably attribute the disparity to fate rather than physiology.
clips.text_en_c2: My identical twin and I have, in a fit of rigorous autodidacticism, subjected our respective metabolisms to formal scrutiny. Dietary intake, meticulously logged, yields identical caloric measurements; macronutrient composition—fat, protein, carbohydrate—is indistinguishable between us. We even ventured to collect and incinerate our faeces, an exercise whose indignity was compensated only by the revelation that residual caloric content remained consistent across samples. Yet I remain, unambiguously, obese, whilst he persists in a state of irritating leanness. My acquaintances proffer metabolic explanations; the local fortune-teller insists upon destiny. I have, faute de mieux, subscribed to both interpretations with equanimity.

clips.text_zh: 唔好睇我，/a/又有老膠話『非処女』角色唔應該接受喎。香港otaku都係咁，30歲single一個人返屋企煲Gundam 00同鬼滅，回帶到凌晨三點。咁我都係『中古品』啦lol。等我考到牌先再諗呢啲。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Dame Ningen no Aishikata. Used goods shouldn't be acceptable in anime/manga. I'm tired of pretending otherwise. Every season there's some shounen protagonist winning the childhood friend after she waited 10 years for him. In real life, by 30 most people are washed up and alone. Anime needs to reflect that reality.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread debating whether 'used' characters belong in anime

signal.rationale: Observational, anime culture rant, no trade

clips.text_en_b2: Dame Ningen no Aishikata. The whole notion that so-called used goods shouldn't be portrayed as viable love interests in anime and manga has worn me down. Every single season some shounen protagonist ends up with the childhood friend who patiently waited a decade for him. In real life, by thirty most people have washed out of the dating pool entirely. Anime ought to start reflecting that grim reality instead of feeding us the same tired fantasy.
clips.text_en_c1: The recurring discourse on anime boards regarding characters who are not virgins being somehow unacceptable partners never fails to exhaust me. The prevailing narrative insists that protagonists deserve childhood sweethearts who have waited a decade in faithful reserve, yet this romanticised framework bears little resemblance to lived reality. Most people approaching thirty, myself very much included, are essentially solitary, returning to empty apartments to marathon Gundam 00 and Demon Slayer until the early hours of the morning. If the metric by which these communities judge fictional heroines were applied to their own demographic, the conclusion would be considerably more uncomfortable.
clips.text_en_c2: The perennial lament from /a/: non-virginal characters ought not to be admissible romantic options within the anime idiom, a position advanced with the righteous indignation peculiar to those who have, by thirty, retreated into solitary domesticity. The trope is wearisome—the childhood friend who waits a decade for the oblivious protagonist, rewarded with devotion that real-world demographics seldom reciprocate. One observes that by the third decade, the statistical probability of such narratives diminishes considerably; the protagonists, like the audience, are largely solitary. I, too, constitute a pre-owned artefact by such criteria. Licence acquisition shall precede any further rumination on the matter.
